tagline: Giga-projects on the water — from Red Sea island resorts to NEOM, built clean from day one.
summary: Saudi Arabia is building entire destinations on the water under Vision 2030: Red Sea Global's luxury resorts spread across dozens of islands, NEOM and its Sindalah leisure island on the Gulf of Aqaba, the historic gateway of Jeddah, and an Eastern Province that sits a short hop from Bahrain. These are greenfield coasts with sovereign capital, a clean-mobility mandate, and no incumbent water tier to displace — the natural home for a foiling fleet specified in from the start.
why_marine_mobility: Saudi Arabia's coastal story is the giga-project. Red Sea Global's resorts are scattered across islands that, like the Maldives, depend entirely on marine transfers; NEOM and Sindalah are purpose-built for clean, on-demand mobility; and the Red Sea and Gulf coasts are stitched together by long trunk corridors no day-boat can run. Navier's Pioneer II flies the intra-resort island transfers and the short cross-water hops — NEOM to Sharm El Sheikh, the Eastern Province to Bahrain — clean and on-demand, while the Quanta-LR's range opens the long giga-project trunks between Red Sea Global, NEOM and Jeddah. Because these coasts are being built now, the foiling tier can be designed in rather than retrofitted.

demand_signals.label: Island-resort transfer dependency
demand_signals.note: Red Sea Global's resorts are spread across dozens of islands and reefs; like the Maldives, nearly every guest arrival ends in a marine transfer — a captive, high-value, recurring water-mobility market.

demand_signals.label: Greenfield clean-mobility mandate
demand_signals.note: NEOM, Sindalah and Oxagon are purpose-built with a zero-emission mobility brief and sovereign (PIF-backed) capital — a market specifying clean marine transport from day one, with no incumbent to displace.

demand_signals.label: Red Sea & Gulf connectivity triangle
demand_signals.note: NEOM sits a short crossing from Egypt's Sharm El Sheikh and the Eastern Province a short hop from Bahrain — cross-water tourism and business corridors today served by long road or air detours.

use_cases.body: Intra-Red Sea Global island transfers: Shura Island and the resort archipelago linked by quiet, dry, emission-free Pioneer II hops — the clean successor to the speedboat shuttle, matched to an ultra-premium clientele.
NEOM to Sharm El Sheikh: a ~26-nm Pioneer II crossing of the Gulf of Aqaba linking NEOM directly to Egypt's established Red Sea resort hub — a sea bridge replacing a long air or road detour.
Eastern Province to Bahrain: a short Pioneer II Gulf hop linking Saudi's industrial-financial east to Manama, an alternative to the congested causeway for premium and business travel.
Red Sea Global to NEOM: a long-range Quanta-LR trunk linking the kingdom's two flagship Red Sea giga-destinations on a single clean hybrid leg no day-boat can serve.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The intra-Red Sea Global resort transfers, NEOM Sindalah marina hops, the NEOM–Sharm El Sheikh crossing (~26 nm) and the Eastern Province–Bahrain hop (~19–21 nm) all sit inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile range at 30 knots — commercial-ready today.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The giga-project trunks — Red Sea Global to NEOM (~197 nm), Red Sea Global to Jeddah (~276 nm) and Jeddah to NEOM (~470 nm) — are Quanta-LR corridors (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+), with the hybrid drivetrain removing any charging-infrastructure dependency on greenfield coasts.

signature_routes.label: Red Sea Global ↔ NEOM — the long-range giga-project trunk
Red Sea Global ↔ Jeddah — Red Sea coastal trunk
NEOM ↔ Sharm El Sheikh — Gulf of Aqaba cross-water hop
Eastern Province ↔ Manama (Bahrain) — Gulf cross-border hop

transit_planning: For a giga-project developer or sovereign operator: specify a clean, all-weather, on-demand foiling tier into the destination from the outset rather than retrofitting one later. Begin with intra-resort island transfers and the short cross-water hops on Pioneer II — commercial today — then add the Red Sea Global–NEOM–Jeddah trunks on Quanta-LR as hybrid range comes online. The proven Maldives model — a multi-vessel fleet serving island resorts at national scale — maps directly onto Red Sea Global.
competitive_landscape: Because these coasts are greenfield, there is largely no incumbent water tier to displace: resort transfers run on speedboats and tenders, and cross-water travel defaults to road causeways or short flights. There is no clean, stabilised, on-demand foiling option. Navier's craft is faster and drier than a speedboat, cleaner than diesel tenders, and — critically — can be written into the destination's mobility plan before alternatives entrench.
regulatory_note: Maritime activity is overseen by the Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani), the Transport General Authority (TGA) and the Border Guard, while NEOM and Red Sea Global operate under their own special economic and development frameworks that streamline new-mobility deployment. Cross-water legs to Egypt and Bahrain involve standard international maritime-border and customs coordination.
seasonality: The Red Sea is warm and largely navigable year-round, with the main constraint being extreme summer heat (Jun–Aug) — managed by air-conditioned cabins — and occasional winter wind; the Gulf coast is hot and humid in summer. A stabilised foiling craft holds comfort and schedule across windy shoulder conditions on both coasts.

precedents.what: The $100M Navier × JIH Global Maldives partnership — a multi-vessel fleet serving island resorts at national scale — is the direct precedent for the Red Sea Global island-transfer model.
Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium water-shuttle model for Saudi's resort coasts.
